summary: NO-SHIP. R-1, R-2, and R-3 are all still open under reproducible inputs or interleavings. The committed 390/390 unit and 129/129 smoke evidence misses these paths. No existing assertion was weakened beyond the authorized N43 comment edit.

findings.title: R-1 still open: a path token makes a broad grouped branch look narrow
findings.body: After expanding grouped alternatives, `isHostBound` still accepts a domain-shaped token anywhere in the branch, including its path. `^(https://ads\.example\.net/|https://.*\.com/path\.example\.net/)` returns `narrow` while matching `https://www.google.com/path.example.net/` and avoiding both `.invalid` probes. RuleForm therefore skips its `wide` confirmation at `src/features/modifications/rule-form.tsx:177`. The added cases at `src/core/url-scope.test.ts:139` omit this path-token shape.
findings.recommendation: Prove host binding from the URL authority portion of every expanded branch, defaulting to `wide` when that cannot be established. Add this counterexample to both the pure-function table and first-save confirmation coverage.

findings.title: R-2 still open: the migration guard is not an atomic CAS
findings.body: Using a FIFO storage fake—the ordering assumption documented by this fix—the sequence `G(initial migration), G(command), G(migration guard), S(command), S(migration)` leaves the stale migrated `Legacy` state after the newer command state was saved. Both reads can observe v1 before either set, so calling `set` immediately after the predicate is not atomic. The regression test avoids this ordering by awaiting `persistState(edited)` completely before releasing migration at `src/platform/stateStore.test.ts:117-123`.
findings.recommendation: Put migration and command read-modify-write operations behind the same FIFO barrier, or introduce a real revision/CAS mechanism. Add a regression where the command read is already queued before the migration guard read.

findings.title: R-3 still open: service-worker ownership does not serialize manifest writers
findings.body: Each delete request independently suspends automatic Backup and then invokes the whole-manifest delete; concurrent message handlers are not queued. Running two current `deleteBackupSnapshot` calls against a valid `[a,b]` manifest left `a` listed after its chunk was removed, reproducing the reverse corrupt-row race. The reentrancy test at `src/runtime/background-bootstrap.test.ts:484` substitutes a delete fake that never touches a manifest, while the adapter fixture at `src/platform/backupStore.test.ts:123` uses invalid `{at, bytes}` entries and never exercises the real manifest-write branch. Literal single-writer ownership is also false because `clearCloudBackups` remains a renderer-side writer at `src/features/backup/backup-panel.tsx:85`. N43 still explicitly steers around concurrency at `scripts/smoke.mjs:4300-4308`.
findings.recommendation: Route every per-target `bk:manifest` mutation—including automatic Backup, snapshot deletion, cloud clearing, and reset—through one service-worker FIFO. Add valid-fixture tests for overlapping deletions and clear-versus-Backup, asserting both manifest entries and chunks remain consistent.

next_steps: Block merge until all three reproduced paths are fixed.
Replace the current race tests with interleavings that exercise the real adapters and valid manifest data.
Re-run the full build, typecheck, unit, and smoke suite and refresh pinned verification evidence.
